html:
SMTO-SKL-0176 — GitHub couldn't find this file to download

GUID: 6061daae-1c4c-5be6-a4ef-9c3b2cd71a2b
Slug: github-artifact-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • SMTO tried to download a file from GitHub, such as a build output or run log, but GitHub couldn't provide it. It may have expired or been deleted, or your GitHub account in SMTO can't see it. Nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On github.com, open the run in the Actions tab and look at its Artifacts section, or open the file in the project, to see if it is still there. GitHub deletes build outputs and logs after a set time, and then they can't be downloaded.
  2. If it has expired, run the automation again on GitHub to produce a new copy, then ask the Agent to download the new one. An expired file can't be restored; only a new run creates a fresh copy.
  3. If the file is there, ask whoever set up your GitHub Account in Parameter Store to check its access key covers this project and Actions. GitHub reports files your access key can't see as not found.

What success looks like

  • The Agent shows the downloaded file in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your GitHub access in SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A GitHub download (Actions artifact, workflow logs, or raw contents) returned 404, or an Actions artifact download returned 410 Gone; the item may not exist, may have expired, or may be inaccessible to the token.

What this means

  • An artifact download returns HTTP 404 or an Actions artifact download returns HTTP 410. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • An artifact download returns HTTP 404 or an Actions artifact download returns HTTP 410.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact artifact ID, expiry and Actions access.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the artifact ID (or run ID for logs, or path and ref for contents) exists in this repository and has not expired; Actions artifacts and logs are deleted after the repository's retention period and then return 410/404. A 404 can also mean the token lacks actions:read (contents:read for raw contents) or repository access.
  • Verify the exact Actions artifact exists, has not expired and is accessible with Actions read permission.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • An authorized download resolves the intended still-available artifact.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
